Subject: Mutual plan & acceptance tests for Redwood eval

Stephanie —

Thanks again for the demo this morning. Leadership here is aligned to move forward with a short, instrumented evaluation, but procurement and our clinical ops team need a clear mutual action plan (MAP) and a definitive list of acceptance tests so we can sign off internally. Specifically, our stakeholders want: 

- A short milestone timeline (weeks to close) with owners on both sides
- Exit gates and pass/fail criteria for the pilot (not just anecdotal success)
- A runnable acceptance test suite we can hand to our SREs & legal
- Any dependencies (network/VPC, data retention, SOC2 evidence) and how they map to decision points

Can you send a concise MAP + acceptance test inventory we can walk through with procurement next Tuesday? We want to avoid open-ended pilots — the goal is to validate latency, inference cost per 10k requests, and a small set of clinical accuracy checks against a 500-record test set.

Best,
Jason
Director, Data & AI
Acme Health

P.S. Looping Priya (clinical ops) and procurement when we have the plan.
From: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai

Cc: sean_gallagher@redwood.ai, marcus_lin@redwood.ai

Jason — great to hear the team is aligned. Attaching a one-page MAP workbook and a lightweight acceptance test doc to make Tuesday's review efficient (MAP_v1.xlsx, TestPlan-Acceptance.md). Below is a concise staging plan you can paste into your procurement deck. Happy to walk through it live.

High-level MAP (2-phase, 5-week path to close)
- Week 0 (prep, owner alignment) — Redwood: stephanie (AM), Sean: pre-prod infra; Acme: Priya (clinical owner), Procurement lead (contract owner). Deliverable: Signed MAP + network kickoff.
- Weeks 1–2 (pilot run, instrumentation) — Goal: run 2k inference sessions against your masked test set. Acceptance checks executed by Acme SRE & Redwood. Deliverable: Pilot results packet, token-cost breakdown, latency p95/p50.
- Week 3 (acceptance review & security evidence) — Run acceptance tests (see TestPlan). Exit gates: pass on critical security checks (transport encryption, KMS integration), and pilot metrics within agreed thresholds (latency <= 250ms p95, avg cost < $0.20/1k tokens for this workload).
- Week 4 (remediation & re-test window) — If any critical item fails, owners have one sprint for fixes and re-test.
- Week 5 (decision & contract close) — Executive signoff or rollback. Deliverable: Mutual acceptance doc and SOW signature.

Acceptance tests (summary)
- Performance: run 500 synthetic sessions scaled to expected concurrency, capture p50/p95/p99 and tail latencies.
- Cost: token accounting for representative prompts; Redwood provides cost simulation and billing projection.
- Quality: concordance check on 500-record clinical set; target F1 >= 0.82 on annotated labels (per the agreed label schema).
- Reliability: 48-hour soak with KV cache enabled, watch for memory growth/leaks.
- Security & compliance: verify TLS endpoints, KMS key usage, and IP allowlist. Provide SOC2 artifact links.

Exit gates (explicit)
- Hard fail: discovered plaintext PHI in logs, SOC2-required control missing, or data egress misconfiguration.
- Soft fail: metrics outside thresholds but fixable within remediation window — triggers Week 4 re-test.

Operational notes
- Data flows: masked test set only; no production PHI allowed during pilot.
- Audit logs: Redwood will provide a 30-day audit-log export as CSV for the pilot.
- Rollback: simple API key revocation and cached KV flush will fully cut inference access.

I've kept the workbook simple — it maps each acceptance test to an owner, required evidence, and a pass/fail checkbox. For Tuesday, recommend a 30-minute walkthrough and then procurement can confirm the contract language we need.

Attachments: MAP_v1.xlsx, TestPlan-Acceptance.md

Thanks — I can join the procurement call Tuesday at 10am PT if that works.

—Stephanie Nguyen
